text: I think he’s a very sensible man. But why did you sit back there, Agnes,” she added, “and talk so little?” “Because you talked so well, mamma, I thought you required no assistance from me: and, besides, he was your visitor, not mine.” After that, he often called upon us—several times in the course of a week. He generally addressed most of his conversation to my mother: and no wonder, for she could converse. I almost envied the unfettered, vigorous fluency of her discourse, and the strong sense evinced by everything she said—and yet, I did not; for, though I occasionally regretted my own deficiencies for his sake, it gave me very great pleasure to sit and hear the two beings I loved and honoured above every one else in the world, discoursing together so amicably, so wisely, and so well. I was not always silent, however; nor was I at all neglected.
